rules.banned_because: Someone else's names, kept out of everything Euphonia publishes (Appendix E; setting/ip-review.md).
rules.fey_type_because: "Fey" survives only as the creature type; the setting's prose says "fae" (Book Two, What's Different).

items.name: Court Astrologer's Astrolabe
items.text:
Brass plates engraved for one city's latitude, with a rete of stars and a sighting rule.

When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 10 minutes with the astrolabe to find the day's **auspicious hour**: the DM tells you when it falls (or roll a d12: it falls that many hours after dawn). During that hour, you can cast *Bless* from the astrolabe once without expending a spell slot; cast this way, it doesn't require Concentration and lasts until the hour ends. You also have Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) and Intelligence (History) checks about omens, calendars and the heavens during the hour. The astrolabe's owner decides when the duel is fought, the audience is begged or the window is forced, and the rest of the party moves with them.

The DM can also name the day's **inauspicious hour**, and what the stars say goes wrong in it. Nothing in the rules makes it so; everyone at court believes it anyway.

The Safavid shah was crowned a second time in 1668 because the first hour was judged inauspicious.

items.name: Inoculation Lancet
items.text:
A silver lancet and a sealed vial of matter taken from a mild case. Healers in China and India already do this; Lanternhall hasn't heard of it.

Magic that cures a disease doesn't teach the body anything, so a creature cured by magic can catch the disease again; a creature that survives it the slow way can't.

The lancet gives a creature the slow way, safely. One vial is good for ten inoculations against the disease its vial was taken from. Spend 1 minute inoculating a willing creature against that disease. It falls mildly ill: for 1d4 days it has 1 level of Exhaustion that can't be removed until the illness passes. Then it's immune to that disease for life. If it's cured by magic while the illness runs, it gains no immunity, unless the cure is a Physician's Treatment, which counts as the slow way (*The Classes*, Physician, Level 2: Treatment).

*Diseases to use.* Smallpox is the one the practice was built for. Whether a vial works against measles, or the camp fever that follows every army (typhus), is your table's call, since nobody in 1668 knows. The DM sets each one's save and effects on the model of the core rules' diseases; what matters here is that the party spent the days at Exhaustion before the town's outbreak, and the rival party didn't.

items.name: Iron and Salt
items.text:
Cold iron is no special metal: it's just iron, and its power over the Hidden is that it's mortal, worked by human hands. A **horseshoe** over the door, an **iron nail** in the frame, a **line of salt** across the sill.

Ten minutes of iron and salt wards a room or a small building against Hidden creatures until dawn, and a Hidden creature has to be invited in or succeed on a Charisma saving throw to cross. The rule is in *Life on the Border*, Introduction (The Hidden, in the rules, Iron and salt).

Every village knows this; most households do it every night of the dark half. Forgetting is how stories start.

items.name: Khipu of Record
items.text:
A main cord with pendant cords hanging from it, knotted in a code of position, color and twist. The Inca state runs on these, kept by its *khipukamayuq*.

While you hold the khipu, you can tie a knot in a pendant cord as a Magic action and speak up to 25 words into it. Anyone who holds the khipu and runs a finger over that knot hears the words in your voice. The khipu holds ten such knots; untying one erases it. In addition, you have Advantage on Intelligence checks to recall or reckon numbers, accounts or records you've knotted into it.

A Danae who keeps one finds that its knots and hers feel the same in the hand.

*A living tradition.* Khipu are a real Andean way of keeping records, and some highland communities still hold theirs.

items.name: Mutapan Curiosities

pieces.name: Self-Lighting Lamp
pieces.text: Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for 20 feet more, with no flame and no oil; on or off with a touch.

pieces.name: Cold-Country Stove
pieces.text: A small iron box that warms a room or boils a pot without fuel or smoke.

pieces.name: Water Pump
pieces.text: Lifts water from a well or river by a hand's turn to start it, then keeps lifting for a day.

pieces.name: Singing Bird
pieces.text: A Tiny soapstone-and-wire bird that sings at the hour you set, or chimes an alarm.

pieces.name: Night Watch
pieces.text: A pocket clock that never needs winding and chimes when anyone opens the box it's kept in.

pieces.name: Small Loom
pieces.text: Weaves a plain strip of cloth from thread fed into it, slowly, without a weaver.

pieces.name: Cold Box
pieces.text: Keeps food as cold as a winter cellar.

items.text:
The fashionable rarity of the day: owning one says you have money and reach, and people think they're charming novelties.

Small work only. Each curiosity does one thing, and anyone can start it with a touch. Prices are for Mutapa's capital. Abroad, a curiosity costs five times as much in a Monsoon Road port (Malacca and Aceh are on the Road in all but name), ten times as much in Europe, China or the Americas, and whatever the buyer will bear at a court, or in Japan, where the only ships let in are the Dutch and Chinese at Nagasaki.

| Curiosity | Cost | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Self-Lighting Lamp** | 50 GP | Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for 20 feet more, with no flame and no oil; on or off with a touch. |
| **Cold-Country Stove** | 75 GP | A small iron box that warms a room or boils a pot without fuel or smoke. |
| **Water Pump** | 100 GP | Lifts water from a well or river by a hand's turn to start it, then keeps lifting for a day. |
| **Singing Bird** | 50 GP | A Tiny soapstone-and-wire bird that sings at the hour you set, or chimes an alarm. |
| **Night Watch** | 75 GP | A pocket clock that never needs winding and chimes when anyone opens the box it's kept in. |
| **Small Loom** | 100 GP | Weaves a plain strip of cloth from thread fed into it, slowly, without a weaver. |
| **Cold Box** | 75 GP | Keeps food as cold as a winter cellar. |

*Electrical, not magical.* The platinum inside turns the magic around it into current, and the current does the work. *Detect Magic* doesn't show a curiosity, *Dispel Magic* does nothing to one and an *Antimagic Field* doesn't stop one, which runs on the current it has stored (as a Mhizha's Electrical devices do).

*Drift.* A curiosity drifts out of calibration. When an adventure begins, and whenever a curiosity has been through hard travel or stood inside a spell's area, roll a d6; on a 1, it stops working until it's retuned. A Mhizha retunes one in 10 minutes with Tinker's Tools; anyone a Mhizha taught takes an hour.

items.name: Shewstones
items.text:
A pair of stones, tin-white and mirror-bright, each in its own velvet-lined case. The English name comes from Dee and Kelley's scrying crystal; Mutapa's are platinum ore, and they answer (see The World in 1668, Words Across Distance).

A pair of shewstones works as a pair of Sending Stones: one message of up to 25 words, and its reply, each dawn. They're Rare for what they mean, not for what they do. A pair is never sold for coin; it arrives as a gift from Mutapa's king, through the merchant house that deals in them, with strings.

Handling one bare-handed for months is slow arsenic poisoning (flavor; no rule).

*For the DM.* Every shewstone a foreign court receives from Mutapa may be a listening post. Whether Mutapa can hear through them, and whether anyone has worked out that it might, is a question for your campaign.

items.name: Talisman Papers (fu)
items.text:
A strip of yellow paper written in cinnabar by a Daoist master, in a script meant for spirits rather than people. You paste it on the bed, the sleeper or the cursed thing.

A *fu* holds one spell, written into it. Anyone can use it, whatever their class: paste it on yourself, a willing creature or an object within reach as a Magic action (an unwilling creature can't be papered: put an area spell on an object instead), and the spell takes effect as if cast at its lowest level (an area spell is centered on the paper), with a save DC of 13 and no Concentration (it lasts its full duration or until the paper is torn off). Any creature within reach of the paper can tear it off as a Utilize action, which is how a friend breaks a *Calm Emotions* and how a spirit's servant gets at a sleeper. Common papers hold *Sanctuary*; uncommon ones hold *Protection from Evil and Good*, *Calm Emotions* or *Remove Curse*.

The ones pasted over doors on the fifteenth day of the seventh month are the strongest, or so the masters say.

*A living tradition.* *Fu* are a real part of Daoist practice, written and used today.

items.name: Talismanic Shirt
items.text:
A linen shirt worn under armor, covered inside and out with Qur'anic verse, the names of God and magic squares, begun on a day the stars chose. Ottoman princes and generals wore them into battle.

While you wear the shirt, you have a +1 bonus to saving throws, and once per Long Rest, when you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it and must use the new roll.

*A living tradition.* These shirts are a real part of Islamic learned practice (the science of letters).

items.name: Water-Bearer's Bucket
items.text:
An oak bucket bound in copper, always cold to the touch, with a dipper chained to the handle. Every village on the border has a story about one.

The bucket holds 3 gallons, and it fills itself with cold, clean water at dawn and whenever you finish a Short Rest. Pouring the full bucket over a creature as a Utilize action counts as dousing it with a bucketful of cold water: it cools a Bordermarch Barbarian from the Deep Ríastrad, which spares it the Exhaustion (*Life on the Border*, Bordermarch Barbarian, The Deep Ríastrad), puts out a burning creature and ends any effect a dousing ends.

items.name: Special Commission
items.text: While you're attuned to the locket, no likeness, possession, or body part of yours gives anyone a connection to you for *Scrying* or any other divination; the caster is treated as having no connection at all. In addition, when a scrying sensor appears within 10 feet of you, you know it, and you know which direction it's watching from.

items.name: Cipher Wheel
items.text:
**Reading.** If you study two or more messages written in the same cipher for 1 hour each, the wheel works the cipher out, and you can read anything written in it from then on.

**Writing.** Wheels are made in pairs. A message you write in the wheel's own cipher can be read only by someone holding its twin; to anyone else, magic included, it reads as a merchant's dull letter about wool prices.

items.name: Club Spyglass
items.text: While you hold the spyglass to your eye, you can use Observe on a creature you can see within 300 feet of yourself, and you can read the lips of a creature you can see within that range if you know the language it's speaking.

items.name: Lead-Lined Writing Box
items.text: Papers and objects inside the closed box can't be seen, read, or detected by magic. The box has a lock (DC 18 to pick), and the hidden compartment under the false bottom takes a successful DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check to find.

items.name: Sympathetic Miniature
items.text:
The miniature shows one creature, painted from life. To *Scrying* and any other divination magic that asks how well the caster is connected to its subject, the miniature counts as the strongest connection possible: a body part, a lock of hair, or a bit of nail.

While you hold the miniature and concentrate on it for 1 minute, you know whether its subject is alive, and the direction to it if it's on the same plane as you.

*Court painters are a security risk.* Some courts are learning to commission portraits that are a little wrong on purpose.

items.name: Keepsakes of the Disciplines

attunement.by: a Counsellor of the Keepsake's Subclass

members.name: House Ledger
members.text: In any settlement where your house has standing, once per tenday you can draw on credit up to 50 GP times your Counsellor level without coin changing hands; the house settles it, and you owe the house. While you hold the ledger and handle an object for 1 minute, you know what it last sold for and roughly where.

members.name: Marked Deck
members.text: You have Advantage on any ability check you make with a Gaming Set. In addition, once per Long Rest, when you roll your computation die, you can roll it twice and use either result.

members.name: Mask of Manners
members.text: While you wear the mask (it lies against your face and can't be seen), your face shows whatever expression you choose, and Wisdom (Insight) checks to read you have Disadvantage.

members.name: Skeleton Keys
members.text: You have Advantage on ability checks you make with Thieves' Tools. In addition, once per Long Rest, you can open a nonmagical lock you touch with them, silently and without a check.

members.name: Baton of Command
members.text: Once per Long Rest, when you use Direct, you can choose two allies instead of one. While you hold the baton, troops who can see you know what you want of them without being told.

members.name: Dead Drop
members.text: A pair of small lockboxes, each about the size of a book. You can open one and place up to 1 pound of objects inside; when it's closed, they're in the other box, wherever it is on the same plane. Once you send something, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

items.text:
- **House Ledger (Factor).** In any settlement where your house has standing, once per tenday you can draw on credit up to 50 GP times your Counsellor level without coin changing hands; the house settles it, and you owe the house. While you hold the ledger and handle an object for 1 minute, you know what it last sold for and roughly where.
- **Marked Deck (Gamester).** You have Advantage on any ability check you make with a Gaming Set. In addition, once per Long Rest, when you roll your computation die, you can roll it twice and use either result.
- **Mask of Manners (Hollowed).** While you wear the mask (it lies against your face and can't be seen), your face shows whatever expression you choose, and Wisdom (Insight) checks to read you have Disadvantage.
- **Skeleton Keys (Majordomo).** You have Advantage on ability checks you make with Thieves' Tools. In addition, once per Long Rest, you can open a nonmagical lock you touch with them, silently and without a check.
- **Baton of Command (Marshal).** Once per Long Rest, when you use Direct, you can choose two allies instead of one. While you hold the baton, troops who can see you know what you want of them without being told.
- **Dead Drop (Spymaster).** A pair of small lockboxes, each about the size of a book. You can open one and place up to 1 pound of objects inside; when it's closed, they're in the other box, wherever it is on the same plane. Once you send something, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

items.name: Master's Piece

members.name: Athanor
members.text: Each batch of elixirs you make has one more elixir, of your choice.

members.name: Repair Kit
members.text: Once per Long Rest, as a Utilize action, you touch your construct and it regains Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your Intelligence modifier.

members.name: Spare Barrel
members.text: You can set down your turret one more time before you finish a Long Rest.

members.name: Spare Cell
members.text: Your suit can hold two charges at a time. You release them one at a time.

members.name: Surveyor's Compass
members.text: You have two more folds.

items.text:
Each is made for one subclass and works only for a Mhizha of that subclass.

- *Athanor (Chemist).* Each batch of elixirs you make has one more elixir, of your choice.
- *Repair Kit (Constructor).* Once per Long Rest, as a Utilize action, you touch your construct and it regains Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your Intelligence modifier.
- *Spare Barrel (Gunner).* You can set down your turret one more time before you finish a Long Rest.
- *Spare Cell (Lionskin).* Your suit can hold two charges at a time. You release them one at a time.
- *Surveyor's Compass (Mapmaker).* You have two more folds.

items.name: Tuned Arc Gun
items.text: If you find or craft a Tuned Arc Gun, you can attune to it, and it replaces your Arc Gun (a Lionskin builds it into the suit). You gain a bonus, determined by the item's rarity, to attack rolls with the Arc Gun, your turret, and your construct's Strike, and to the spell attack rolls and spell save DCs of your Mhizha spells. Your Preparations and other Mhizha features that use your spell save DC don't gain it.

items.name: Workshop Coat
items.text: While you wear it, you have a +1 bonus to Armor Class. Once per Long Rest, when you finish a Short Rest, you can rebuild all your devices and regain all your expended Preparations.

items.name: Flea Glass
items.text: Through the flea glass, an object you're holding looks many times its size: you can read writing too small for the eye, find a hairline crack, or see the tool marks on a forged seal. You have Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks to examine an object small enough to hold in one hand.

items.name: Reflecting Telescope
items.text: It works as a Spyglass and fits in a coat pocket.

items.name: The Transactions
items.text: Each month, wherever letters can reach you, the DM tells you one piece of news from the learned world: a discovery, a quarrel, a death, an expedition, or a rumor of what someone is working on. Some of it is wrong.

items.name: Weatherglass
items.text: If you spend 1 minute reading the weatherglass, you know whether a storm is coming within the next 12 hours. It also tells you how high you've climbed, as Pascal's brother-in-law showed on the Puy de Dôme in 1648: you know your height above the sea to within a hundred feet.

items.name: Bonesaw
items.text:
The saw is a magic Greatsword that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. It is your Saw for every Physician feature, and you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells.

- **Serrated.** When you hit a creature with the saw, it bleeds: at the start of each of its turns, it takes 1d6 Slashing damage. The bleeding ends when the creature regains Hit Points, or when any creature within 5 feet of it takes a Utilize action to bind the wound; otherwise it runs until treated, even after the fight. A creature can bleed from the saw only once at a time. Constructs and Undead don't bleed.
- **Through the Bone.** When you use Amputation on a creature you hit with the saw, the creature makes its saving throw with Disadvantage, and you can take a limb in a fight twice between rests instead of once.
- **Rough Work.** When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with the saw, you regain one expended Prowess Die. Once this property has restored a die, it can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

items.name: Doctor's Coat
items.text:
A long coat of close-woven cloth, cut for work, with deep pockets. Blood, filth, and rain don't cling to it, and it takes the cut and color its wearer's discipline would choose: a white coat for a Doctor, a buff coat for a Combat Medic, a long black wrap for a Plague Doctor, an unbleached, hand-stitched coat for a Hedge Witch, an oddly soothing plum-gray for a Neurologist, an apron for a Surgeon or a Chirurgeon, a weathered field coat for a Vitalist, and for an Immortalist, the color of their attuned energy.

You gain these benefits while wearing the coat:

- If you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 15 plus your Dexterity modifier.
- You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects, and you have Immunity to disease and to the Poisoned condition.
- Your spell save DC and spell attack bonus each increase by 2.
- **Attending.** Once on each of your turns, when you restore Hit Points to a creature with a Physician feature or spell, you can use your Diagnosis feature on a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself as part of the same action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.

items.name: Rod of the Doctor
items.text:
A plain rod of dark wood with a single serpent coiled around it. It can be wielded as a magic Mace that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. While you hold it, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells, and it serves as a Healer's Kit that never runs out of uses.

**Absorb Life.** While holding the rod, you can take a Reaction when another creature that isn't hostile to you casts a spell that targets only you. The spell has no effect on you, and the rod gains a number of charges equal to the spell's level. If this brings the rod's charges above 50, the serpent wakes: the rod splits, every creature within 30 feet of you regains Hit Points equal to 4 times the number of charges above 50, and the rod is destroyed.

**Spells.** The rod has 50 charges. While holding it, you can expend charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC and spellcasting ability: *Cure Wounds* (1 charge per spell level, up to 5), *Anaesthesia* (2 charges), *Lesser Restoration* (2 charges), *Aura of Vitality* (3 charges), *Revivify* (3 charges), *Death Ward* (4 charges), *Greater Restoration* (5 charges), *Mass Cure Wounds* (5 charges), *Raise Dead* (5 charges), *Defibrillation* (6 charges), *Heal* (6 charges), or *Regenerate* (7 charges). Material components with a cost must still be provided.

The rod's charges won't do harm. When you cast *Defibrillation* from it, you can choose only the Start effect for each creature.

You can also cast the following from the rod without expending charges: *Detect Magic*, *Detect Poison and Disease*, *Guidance*, *Light*, *Mage Hand*, *Prestidigitation*, *Purify Food and Drink*, and *Spare the Dying*.

**Steady the Hand.** When you use your Healing Prowess feature, you can expend 1 charge instead of a Prowess Die. You can do this no more than once on each of your turns.

**Regaining Charges.** The rod regains 4d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 20, the rod regains 1d12 + 1 charges.

**Last Breath.** You can take a Magic action to snap the rod in two. The rod is destroyed and releases everything in it in a 30-foot Emanation originating from you. Each creature of your choice in the Emanation regains Hit Points equal to 6 times the number of charges the rod had, and each such creature that died within the last minute returns to life with those Hit Points instead. You then drop to 0 Hit Points and are Stable, and you can't regain Hit Points until you finish a Long Rest.

items.name: The Ward
items.text:
A round shield of pale wood banded in brass, with a lamp-glass boss that burns without oil.

While attuned to the shield, you have Shield training. The shield hovers beside you rather than hanging on your arm: you don't need a free hand to benefit from it, and you can perform the Somatic components of spells as if you weren't wielding it. A creature can't benefit from this shield and another Shield at once.

- **Lamp.** The boss sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet, in the color of your Doctor's Coat if you are wearing one and pale gold if you aren't. A creature in the Bright Light can't be hidden from you.
- **Bedside.** As a Bonus Action, you can send the shield to hover beside a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. While it is there, the shield's AC bonus applies to that creature instead of you, and the Lamp moves with it. If the creature is your patient and is Bloodied, the first time on each turn it would take damage from an attack, you can take a Reaction to reduce that damage by one roll of your Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier (no die is expended). The shield returns to you as a Bonus Action, or on its own if the creature is ever more than 60 feet from you.

items.name: Atlas of Roads
items.text:
A folding chart that never folds the same way twice, with leaves that unfold upward into the Outer Planes. Every road you have walked in spirit is inked on it, and some you haven't yet. You can use the atlas as a Spellcasting Focus for your Revelator spells. While it's on your person, you gain a bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your Revelator spells and features. Your Planar Strike uses your spell attack modifier, so it gains the bonus too. The bonus is determined by the atlas's rarity.

**Another Road.** While you carry the atlas, you have one extra Favor.

items.name: The Inked Wheel
items.text:
A series of planar tattoos, one for each plane, each inked on that plane by a native of it. The artifact begins as a single tattoo of the Middle World (the Material Plane) over your heart. It is a Spellcasting Focus for your Revelator spells that needs no hand, and while you are attuned to it, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your Revelator spells and features. Your Planar Strike uses your spell attack modifier, so it gains the bonus too. This bonus doesn't stack with the Atlas of Roads.

**The Skin Remembers.** Whenever you walk a plane (see "Soul's Journey"), a tattoo of it appears somewhere on your body, and stays. Once per Long Rest for each tattoo, you can open a vista to that plane without spending a Favor, if you know its Revelation.

**Opposite Shores.** While you bear tattoos of two planes on opposite sides of the Wheel (such as Elysium and Asphodel, the Celestial Bureaucracy and Limbo, or Svarga and the Nine Circles), you have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Charmed or Frightened condition, and to avoid being moved to another plane against your will.

**Marked.** Natives of every plane whose tattoo you bear recognize what you are on sight. They needn't like you for it.

**Destroying the Wheel.** The tattoos can't be removed by any magic short of *Wish*, and they return if the skin they're on is lost. They fade only when their bearer has walked every plane in the Cosmography, and then they leave behind a single tattoo of the whole Wheel, which grants nothing at all.

items.name: Pathway Keepsakes

attunement.by: a Revelator of the Keepsake's Pathway

members.text: A stone from the bridge, worn smooth on one side by every traveler
A stoppered vial of river water that never runs dry
A laurel leaf of beaten gold
An obol that is always cold, and is never the fare
A twig of ash that stays in leaf

items.text:
Each pathway has its keepsake, a little of its earth end carried home.

| Pathway | Keepsake |
|---|---|
| The Bridge | A stone from the bridge, worn smooth on one side by every traveler |
| The River of Life | A stoppered vial of river water that never runs dry |
| The Mountain | A laurel leaf of beaten gold |
| The River of Death | An obol that is always cold, and is never the fare |
| The Tree | A twig of ash that stays in leaf |

While you carry the keepsake, you have one extra Favor.

items.name: Repeating Crossbow
items.text:
A traveler's crossbow with a box magazine above the stock, cocked and fired with a single lever. You gain a bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, determined by its rarity. It doesn't have the Loading property.

**Magazine.** The crossbow holds ten bolts. You don't need a free hand to draw ammunition from it, and you can refill it as a Utilize action.

**Volley (Rare Only).** When you take the Attack action with the crossbow, you can empty the magazine instead of making your attacks: make one attack against each creature of your choice (up to five) within 10 feet of a point you can see within the weapon's normal range, using a separate bolt for each. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

items.name: Walker's Strides
items.text:
Traveling boots the color of the Border Ethereal, gray on gray. Wherever they've walked, there are footprints on the far side of the Veil. You gain these benefits while wearing them:

- You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
- Your spell save DC and spell attack modifier each increase by 2. This stacks with the Atlas of Roads or the Inked Wheel.
- Your Visiting Spirits have a +2 bonus to Armor Class.

**Weather of the Plane.** While you have a vista open, you have Resistance to the damage type your Planar Strike deals.

**Walk Between.** You ignore Difficult Terrain, including the Difficult Terrain of moving through creatures and objects during Ethereal Stride. Once per Short or Long Rest, you can use Ethereal Stride without spending a Favor.

items.name: Wayfarer's Cloak
items.text:
A traveler's cloak of no particular color, patched in a dozen fabrics from a dozen worlds. While you wear the cloak, you gain the following benefits. The cloak protects you from a plane's environment, never from its nature: it does nothing against the hazards described in "What the Walk Costs."

**Weatherproof.** You stay dry in rain and snow, and you ignore the effects of Extreme Cold and Extreme Heat.

**Any Air.** You can breathe normally at any altitude and in smoke, dust, or stale air, and you ignore the effects of High Altitude.

**Inner Pocket.** The cloak has an extradimensional pocket that holds one object weighing no more than 1 pound, such as a map, a key, or a vial. Only you can find the pocket, and you can stow or draw its object as part of any action.

items.name: Wayfarer's Staff
items.text:
A walking stick worn smooth at the grip and notched along its length. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

**Trail-Wise.** While you carry the staff, you can't become lost except by magic, and you always know which way is north and the way back to where you finished your last Long Rest, if it's on the same plane.

**Sure Footing.** While you carry the staff, you and up to six creatures traveling with you ignore Difficult Terrain made of natural ground, such as mud, scree, snow, or undergrowth, during overland travel.

**Spells.** The staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can expend charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: *Alarm*, *Comprehend Languages*, *Create or Destroy Water*, *Feather Fall*, *Longstrider*, or *Purify Food and Drink* (1 charge); *Locate Object* or *Pass without Trace* (2 charges); *Tiny Hut*, *Tongues*, or *Water Walk* (3 charges); or *Locate Creature* (4 charges). If you expend the staff's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff becomes a nonmagical quarterstaff.

items.name: Basalt of Nan Madol
items.text: While you hold it, you can cast *Elementalism* with it, and when you touch worked stone you know roughly how long ago it was set and whether magic shaped it. A Circle of Shapers Druid can use it as a Druidic Focus.

items.name: Origin Stones

members.name: Seam Stone
members.text: Heavy for its size; you always know which way is north and which way is down, and you never lose your footing on loose stone or a ship's deck.

members.name: Hearthstone
members.text: Warm to hold; lights a fire on a touch; you're comfortable in any cold down to freezing.

members.name: Rime Stone
members.text: Always cold; keeps a box of food fresh; you're comfortable in any heat a person could survive.

members.name: Lodestone
members.text: You can lift twice as much as your Strength allows, for 1 minute at a time.

members.name: Sunstone
members.text: Sheds Dim Light in a 10-foot radius on command; through it, you can find the sun on a clouded day.

members.name: Thunder Egg
members.text: You know the weather for the next 24 hours where you are.

items.text:
A stone that carries a little of a plane. Each is keyed to one origin, and it gives its holder a quality-of-life knack:

- **Seam Stone (Earth).** Heavy for its size; you always know which way is north and which way is down, and you never lose your footing on loose stone or a ship's deck.
- **Hearthstone (Fire).** Warm to hold; lights a fire on a touch; you're comfortable in any cold down to freezing.
- **Rime Stone (Frost).** Always cold; keeps a box of food fresh; you're comfortable in any heat a person could survive.
- **Lodestone (Kinetic).** You can lift twice as much as your Strength allows, for 1 minute at a time.
- **Sunstone (Light).** Sheds Dim Light in a 10-foot radius on command; through it, you can find the sun on a clouded day.
- **Thunder Egg (Storm).** You know the weather for the next 24 hours where you are.

items.name: Pressure Gauge

attunement.by: a Sorcerer of an Origin in This Chapter

items.text: While you wear the gauge, its needle steadies whoever stands near you: allies within 10 feet of you have Advantage on saving throws against your Overflow. Once per Long Rest, when your Pressure would increase, you can choose to keep it where it is.

items.name: Sealed Letter
items.text: Once per Long Rest, you can break the seal (it reseals at dawn) to call an angel as Call an Angel does, at Rank 2 (the table's level 3–4 row), without expending a spell slot. It counts as your angel for that fight, under Call an Angel's one-angel limit. In addition, a letter you write and seal with the same wax reaches its addressee by the next dawn, wherever on the plane they are, if they're willing to receive it.

items.name: Mason's Square and Compasses
items.text: While you hold them, you can inscribe your Figures one more time before you need to rest, and you can measure any distance you can see to the inch. In addition, you can spend 10 minutes with them to lay out a building, a road, or a camp so that its lines are true: for 24 hours, the place can't be thin ground, and no creature can teleport into or out of it except to or from a space in one of its doorways. Once you do this, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

items.name: Lahore Astrolabe
items.text: In your hands, the astrolabe tells the hour by day or night, your latitude, the direction and rough distance of any city engraved on its plates (Mecca is always engraved), and the hours of prayer for the place you stand.

items.name: Dream's Mantle
items.text:
This cloak never hangs the same way twice. It is dew-heavy one hour and dry as leaves the next, and it turns with the seasons your warps carry. You gain these benefits while wearing it:

- You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
- You gain a +1 bonus to the attack rolls and saving throw DCs of your Danae spells and features. The mantle isn't a focus, so this adds to the bonus of a Danae focus you're holding.

**The Season Lingers.** When you give a warp a season, the mantle takes on that season until you give a warp another.

| Season | While the Mantle Holds It |
|---|---|
| Spring | Your Speed increases by 10 feet, and you have Resistance to Poison damage. |
| Summer | You have Resistance to Fire and Radiant damage. |
| Autumn | You have Advantage on Charisma checks, and you have Resistance to Psychic damage. |
| Winter | You have Resistance to Cold damage. |

items.name: Tokens of Method

attunement.by: a Danae of the Token's Subclass

members.text: A spool of gray thread that can't be cut
A die with a seventh face that only you have ever seen it land on
A skeleton key that fits any lock once, and every lock it has fitted ever after
An uncut ogham stave that warms near a lie
A mason's lodestone that pulls toward bedrock

items.text:
Each method has its token, the subclass's warp made solid.

| Subclass | Token |
|---|---|
| Binding | A spool of gray thread that can't be cut |
| Changing | A die with a seventh face that only you have ever seen it land on |
| Crossing | A skeleton key that fits any lock once, and every lock it has fitted ever after |
| Naming | An uncut ogham stave that warms near a lie |
| Shaping | A mason's lodestone that pulls toward bedrock |

The token is what the table says, and its oddity is real (the thread won't cut, the stave does warm), but it does nothing in play beyond what follows.

When you have no warps left, you can draw on the token (no action required) to regain one expended warp. Once the token is drawn on, it can't be drawn on again until the next dawn.

items.name: Wyrdwright's Tools
items.text:
A set of tools from the Danae's tool list, or a Danae subclass's tool, worked in fae material: a mason's chisel of moonstone, a weaver's shuttle that hums when it's idle, dice that are warm to the touch. You can use the tools as a Spellcasting Focus for your Danae spells. While holding them, you gain a bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your Danae spells and features. The bonus is determined by the tools' rarity. It doesn't stack with another Danae focus's bonus to spell attacks or DCs; if more than one applies, use the highest.

**Deep Well.** While you're attuned to the tools, the number of warps you can make between rests increases by 1.

**Fine Weaving.** When you use Fae Weaving with these tools, each object can be worth up to 20 GP × your Danae level.

items.name: Hero-Light Torc

place.section: Barbarian Subclass: Path of the Bordermarch

items.text: While you wear the torc, your allies always know where you stand with the Deep Ríastrad: it glows red while it lasts, and white when you're cooled. When you're cooled from the Deep Ríastrad, you regain Hit Points equal to your Barbarian level.

items.name: Green Mantle

place.section: Barbarian Subclass: Path of the Faebreaker

items.text: While you hold a creature by Hold a Friend and it's wrapped in the mantle, it has Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed and Frightened conditions. When you hold a creature through The Night Turns wrapped in the mantle, the night is won at midnight rather than at dawn.

items.name: Fiddle of the Hill
items.text: While you play the fiddle, the first thing you remember with Remembering after each Long Rest doesn't go on your tally, and creatures that hear it play for 1 minute or more have Disadvantage on saving throws against being Charmed by you. In addition, you can set the fiddle playing on its own for up to 1 hour: anyone who dances to it doesn't tire, and doesn't notice the time.

items.name: Adder Stone
items.text: While you hold the stone to your eye (raising it takes a Bonus Action, and it keeps that hand busy), you see Hidden creatures within 60 feet of you in their true forms, through any illusion, glamour, or shape-change, and you can see Hidden creatures within that range that have the Invisible condition. A Cleric of the Hidden Domain who carries it also has Advantage on the first Charisma (Persuasion) check of each bargain.

items.name: Fairy Doctor's Bottle
items.text: You can spend 1 minute looking into the bottle to ask the Hidden a question about one creature or place you can see: the bottle shows you the answer as *Augury* would, or tells you whether the creature has been taken, swapped, or elf-shot, and by whom. Once used, the bottle can't be used again until the next dawn. If the bottle is ever smashed, everything it has shown you is forgotten.

items.name: Iron Bell
items.text: As a Magic action, you can ring the bell. Until the end of your next turn, each Hidden creature of your choice within 60 feet of you that can hear it loses the Invisible condition, can't gain it, and can't teleport. You can ring it this way a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest. Rung at a door, it also tells you whether a Hidden creature has crossed that threshold since the last dawn.

items.name: Elf-Arrow
items.text: Worn as an amulet, the arrowhead brings its wearer home: if it's Taken, it has Advantage on the saving throws it repeats to find its way back. Dipped in water, it makes that water a cure: a creature that drinks it loses the Poisoned condition, and a creature Hidden magic made sick is cured of it. Once the arrowhead makes a cure, it can't do so again until the next dawn. A Mortal Hunter who carries one as a token also has Advantage on checks to track the creature it last shot with Elf-Shot.

items.name: Fairy Bridle
items.text: As a Magic action, you can shake the bridle to call a horse of the Hunt: it acts as the steed of *Phantom Steed* for 8 hours, except that it can run over water and through standing crops as if they were open ground, and it leaves no tracks. Once you call one, you can't do so again until the next dawn. Riders of the Hunt know the bells and leave you alone if you ride with them.

items.name: Fairy Cup
items.text: When you drink from the cup as you finish a Short Rest, you regain one expended use of Step into the Hidden, and you can't gain the Charmed condition until your next Long Rest. While the cup is unbroken in your household, the DM can grant the household a small piece of luck once a month. If it breaks, the luck runs out at once, and the DM decides what that costs.

weapons.name: Bagh nakh
weapons.change: Slashing, not Thrown; concealable in a closed hand

weapons.name: Combination weapon
weapons.change: a pocket pistol in the hilt, concealable as the hilt; one shot (see below)

weapons.name: Katar
weapons.change: strapped to the hand: nothing can make you drop it while you're conscious

weapons.name: Pocket pistol
weapons.change: a screw-barrel flintlock; fires Firearm Bullets; loud (audible for 300 feet); concealable in a pocket or a muff

weapons.name: Stonebow
weapons.change: Bludgeoning; quiet; fires lead balls or pebbles (use Sling Bullets); can knock a creature out (see below)
